concept.name: Gap up
concept.definition: A gap in which a session's low is higher than the previous session's high, leaving an untraded void below the new session's range. Generally read as a sign of strong buying interest; its analytical meaning depends on where in the trend or pattern it occurs.
concept.intuition: Demand overwhelmed supply overnight, so the market had to reopen above yesterday's entire trading range.
concept.mechanics: Identified when today's low exceeds yesterday's high on the chart. Interpretation follows gap typology: in a congestion area it may be a common gap, breaking out of a range a breakaway gap, mid-trend a runaway gap, and late in an extended move a possible exhaustion gap.
concept.failure_modes: Gap ups into extended moves can be exhaustion gaps that mark the top; and opening gaps that fail to hold through the close are just intraday volatility, not structural gaps.
concept.misconceptions: That a gap up is automatically bullish follow-through fuel; context decides, and faded gaps are a daily occurrence in thin markets.
concept.example: After weeks of consolidation, a stock gaps above its range resistance on heavy volume following earnings — a bullish breakaway-style gap up.

citations.source: StockCharts ChartSchool — Gaps and Gap Analysis
